practices.conditioning_and_openness: Describe a specific situation before linking it to an undefined center.
practices.relationships_and_circuitry: Discuss boundaries and expectations directly instead of inferring them from channels.
practices.life_theme: Check the four cross activations against the Personality and Design Sun/Earth rows.
practices.variables_and_transference: If birth time is uncertain, compare variable results across the plausible time range.
practices.gates_and_lines: Read a gate together with its center, line, activating planet, and completed channels.
practices.integration: Keep only claims that refer to a visible calculation or a recorded observation.

types.generator: Consistent sacral energy is central; satisfaction grows through clear response.
types.manifesting_generator: Sacral response and fast movement combine; clarity improves when action follows response.
types.manifestor: Initiating energy is central; informing others reduces resistance around independent action.
types.projector: Focused guidance is central; recognition and timing shape where energy lands well.
types.reflector: Openness is central; time and environment reveal what is reliable.
types.fallback: This type describes how energy meets the world.

authorities.emotional: Emotional authority favors waiting for the wave to settle before deciding.
authorities.sacral: Sacral authority favors body-level yes/no response in the moment.
authorities.splenic: Splenic authority favors quiet, immediate instinct.
authorities.ego_projected: Ego authority tracks promises, will, and what can honestly be sustained.
authorities.self_projected: Self-projected authority clarifies through speaking from identity and direction.
authorities.sounding_board: Mental authority clarifies through trusted environments and reflection.
authorities.lunar: Lunar authority needs time and repeated conditions before clarity forms.
authorities.fallback: Authority describes the decision signal to privilege.

human_design.planet_activation_summary: {planet} carries this gate through the {layer} layer.

generator.summary: Generators have a defined Sacral and no motor-to-Throat link. The framework describes sustainable life-force that works best when it is spent on things that draw a genuine response.
generator.guidance: Notice what you feel pulled toward, commit where your gut says yes, and let the rest pass without forcing it.

manifesting_generator.summary: Manifesting Generators combine a defined Sacral with a motor connected to the Throat. The framework describes quick, multi-directional energy that responds first and then moves swiftly, often skipping steps.
manifesting_generator.guidance: Respond first, then tell the people your move affects. Expect to change course when something stops feeling right.

manifestor.summary: Manifestors have a motor connected to the Throat and an undefined Sacral. The framework describes an initiating energy that acts on its own impulse and often meets resistance when others are caught off guard.
manifestor.guidance: Before you act, say what you are about to do. Informing clears the path and eases friction with people nearby.

projector.summary: Projectors have an undefined Sacral and no motor connected to the Throat. The framework describes a gift for seeing others and systems clearly, and for guiding, rather than for sustained doing.
projector.guidance: Offer big guidance where you are recognized and invited. Rest generously, since your energy is not meant to be constant.

reflector.summary: Reflectors have no defined centers. The framework describes someone who samples and mirrors the surrounding people and places, and whose clarity builds slowly as the Moon moves through the whole wheel.
reflector.guidance: Give major decisions about a lunar cycle of time, talk them through with trusted people, and choose your surroundings with care.

emotional.how: Clarity is said to come over time as the emotional wave rises and falls, never from a single moment of intensity.
emotional.practice: Sleep on decisions, wait for the wave to settle, and notice whether the answer stays steady.

sacral.how: Decisions come from an immediate, bodily gut response to something in front of you, such as an expansive or a contracting feeling.
sacral.practice: Ask yes-or-no questions out loud or to yourself and notice the sound or sensation of the answer.

splenic.how: A quiet, spontaneous, in-the-moment knowing about what is healthy for you. It speaks once and does not repeat itself.
splenic.practice: Pay attention to the first subtle impression and act on it, rather than waiting for it to come back.

ego_manifested.how: Willpower speaks through the Throat. The framework points to what you truly want and are willing to commit to.
ego_manifested.practice: Say out loud what you want and can follow through on, then inform the people it affects.

ego_projected.how: Willpower is processed by speaking with trusted people. Hearing yourself talk about what you want reveals what you can actually commit to.
ego_projected.practice: Talk through a decision with someone you trust and listen to your own words as you speak.

self_projected.how: Identity and direction become clear by speaking aloud. The voice itself, not the listener's reply, is where the answer shows up.
self_projected.practice: Voice your thoughts to a trusted sounding board and listen for what rings true to you.

sounding_board.how: There is no inner authority. Clarity is said to emerge from talking with trusted people and from the quality of your surroundings.
sounding_board.practice: Discuss decisions with people you trust, in different settings, and notice where you feel clear.

lunar.how: Clarity builds slowly across a full lunar cycle, as each Moon gate passes through the undefined chart and offers a different view.
lunar.practice: Revisit major decisions over about 28 days and compare how they feel as the cycle moves.

none.summary: No center is defined, which is the Reflector pattern. Every center is open to the surroundings, and there is no fixed internal connection to rely on.

single.summary: All defined centers are connected in one group, so the energy flows within a single, self-contained circuit and feels internally consistent.

split.summary: Two separate defined areas are not linked to each other. The framework suggests seeking people, places, or gates that bridge the gap.

triple_split.summary: Three separate defined areas are not linked to each other. The framework describes a need for more varied company and time to feel connected.

quad_split.summary: Four separate defined areas are not linked to each other. The framework describes a need for plenty of variety and time to integrate your different parts.

split_size.small: A small split can be closed by single outside gates, usually in the company of another person or a passing transit.
split_size.large: A large split needs a whole outside channel to close at least one gap, so connection tends to take longer or more deliberate company.

bridge.summary: A bridge is a gate or channel, from another person or a transit, that links separate defined areas for as long as it is present.

1_3.name: Investigator / Martyr
1_3.summary: Studies deeply to build a solid base of knowledge, then tests it in practice. Mistakes become information, and the combination tends toward resilient, experiential learning.

1_4.name: Investigator / Opportunist
1_4.summary: Researches thoroughly and shares what is learned with a close circle. Trusted relationships carry the message, and a secure foundation matters before speaking out.

2_4.name: Hermit / Opportunist
2_4.summary: Natural gifts show up when called on, and solitude restores them. A familiar network tends to recognize the talent and open doors.

2_5.name: Hermit / Heretic
2_5.summary: Private, natural talents that others project hopes onto. Practical results earn trust, while retreat protects the gift from outside expectations.

3_5.name: Martyr / Heretic
3_5.summary: Learns by experimenting and adjusting. What survives the experiments becomes practical wisdom that others may look to for solutions.

3_6.name: Martyr / Role Model
3_6.summary: Lives through bold trial and error before gaining perspective. The three-stage life arc turns experience into objectivity and guidance later on.

4_6.name: Opportunist / Role Model
4_6.summary: Builds influence through relationships and moves through three life phases. Warmth and network come first, with a more observant, exemplary stance growing over time.

4_1.name: Opportunist / Investigator
4_1.summary: The only juxtaposition profile. A firm foundation of knowledge is shared through a familiar network, with a fixed, steady approach to life.

5_1.name: Heretic / Investigator
5_1.summary: Others expect practical solutions, and a well-researched foundation helps meet them. Projection from the outside can be heavy, so reliability matters.

5_2.name: Heretic / Hermit
5_2.summary: Natural gifts that others project onto and call upon. Alone time protects the talent, while delivering practically builds trust.

6_2.name: Role Model / Hermit
6_2.summary: A three-phase life path with natural gifts. Observation from a little distance matures into guidance, and withdrawal helps keep a clear view.

6_3.name: Role Model / Martyr
6_3.summary: A three-phase life path shaped by experimentation. Early trial and error eventually grows into objective, grounded guidance.

1.name: Investigator
1.summary: Builds a secure foundation through study and preparation. Feeling safe in what you understand is the line's central theme.

2.name: Hermit
2.summary: Natural, unforced talent that tends to be recognized by others. It appears when called on and needs withdrawal to restore.

3.name: Martyr
3.summary: Learns through trial and error and adapts to what does not work. Experience, including mistakes, becomes lasting practical knowledge.

4.name: Opportunist
4.summary: Connects through a trusted network and shared influence. Opportunities tend to arrive through familiar relationships.

5.name: Heretic
5.summary: Meets projections and expectations from others. Practical, universal solutions earn trust, while unmet expectations can draw criticism.

6.name: Role Model
6.summary: Moves from experimentation to observation to exemplary guidance. Objectivity and long perspective are the line's hallmark.

trial.summary: From birth to about age 30. The line 6 life resembles line 3: learning by trying things, making mistakes, and gathering experience.

roof.summary: From about 30 to 50, after the Saturn return. A symbolic move onto the roof, observing life from a distance with more objectivity.

role_model.summary: From about 50, after the Chiron return. The framework describes stepping down from the roof, sharing hard-won perspective, and living what you know.

head.biology: Symbolically linked to the pineal gland.
head.role: Pressure to think; the source of inspiration and questions.
head.defined: A steady, consistent way of being inspired and posing questions.
head.undefined: Takes in others' mental pressure and may chase questions that are not its own.
head.not_self_question: Am I trying to answer questions that are not mine?
head.healthy: Knows which questions are worth pursuing and lets the rest go.

ajna.biology: Symbolically linked to the hypothalamus and pituitary.
ajna.role: Conceptualizing: forming opinions, ideas, and mental frameworks.
ajna.defined: A fixed, reliable way of processing and holding ideas.
ajna.undefined: Flexible thinking that can try on many views, and may pretend to be certain.
ajna.not_self_question: Am I pretending to be certain?
ajna.healthy: Holds ideas lightly and values the freedom to see many sides.

throat.biology: Symbolically linked to the thyroid and parathyroid.
throat.role: Expression and manifestation: where energy becomes words and action.
throat.defined: A consistent, recognizable way of speaking and acting.
throat.undefined: Expression varies with company and may reach for attention.
throat.not_self_question: Am I speaking or acting just to be noticed?
throat.healthy: Speaks and acts when the moment genuinely calls for it.

g.biology: Symbolically linked to the liver and blood.
g.role: Identity, direction, and the experience of love.
g.defined: A steady sense of self and direction.
g.undefined: Identity and direction shift with place and company and are sensitive to surroundings.
g.not_self_question: Am I forcing an identity or a direction instead of trusting the right place and people?
g.healthy: Finds direction through being in the right place with the right people.

ego.biology: Symbolically linked to the heart, stomach, gallbladder, and thymus.
ego.defined: A reliable pool of willpower for promises and effort.
ego.undefined: Willpower is not consistent, so there is a pull to prove worth.
ego.not_self_question: Do I have something to prove?
ego.healthy: Knows its worth without needing to prove it.

solar_plexus.biology: Symbolically linked to the kidneys, pancreas, prostate, nervous system, and lungs.
solar_plexus.role: Emotions and feeling; waves of mood that bring clarity over time.
solar_plexus.defined: An emotional wave that moves through highs and lows.
solar_plexus.undefined: Absorbs and amplifies others' emotions and may avoid conflict.
solar_plexus.not_self_question: Am I avoiding a truth or a confrontation to keep the peace?
solar_plexus.healthy: Stays steady around strong emotions and can name truth gently.

spleen.biology: Symbolically linked to the spleen, lymph, and T-cells.
spleen.role: Intuition, immediate awareness, and a sense of what is healthy.
spleen.defined: A spontaneous, reliable sense of what is safe and healthy.
spleen.undefined: Takes in others' fears and holds on to what no longer serves.
spleen.not_self_question: Am I holding on to something that is not good for me?
spleen.healthy: Lets go in time and trusts its own sense of what is good for it.

sacral.biology: Symbolically linked to the ovaries and testes.
sacral.role: Life force, vitality, and the capacity to respond and work.
sacral.defined: A dependable source of energy for work and response.
sacral.undefined: Energy is borrowed from others and may be spent past its limit.
sacral.not_self_question: Do I know when enough is enough?
sacral.healthy: Knows when to stop and rest, borrowing energy without overspending it.

root.role: Adrenaline pressure and the drive to get things done.
root.defined: A steady engine of pressure and momentum.
root.undefined: Takes in others' urgency and may rush to be free of pressure.
root.not_self_question: Am I rushing to get rid of pressure?
root.healthy: Handles pressure calmly and works at its own pace.

defined.label: Defined
defined.summary: Connected by a complete channel, so the center works in a steady, repeatable way that feels familiar and is a consistent part of how you operate.

undefined.label: Undefined
undefined.summary: Has a hanging gate but no complete channel. It is open to the surroundings, and it can be a carrier of conditioning and, with time, of wisdom.

open.label: Open
open.summary: No gate is activated here at all. The center is fully open, and the framework suggests it is especially receptive to its surroundings.

digestion.summary: Read from the Design Sun and called Determination. Symbolically describes the conditions under which the body takes in food and sensory input comfortably.

environment.summary: Read from the Design North Node. Symbolically describes the kinds of surroundings in which the body feels settled and well supported.

motivation.summary: Read from the Personality Sun and also called Awareness. Describes the underlying driver behind choices and what keeps you moving.

perspective.summary: Read from the Personality North Node and also called View. Describes the lens through which you see and focus on the world.

1.summary: Appetite: how foods are combined, either one thing at a time or in a mix.

2.summary: Taste: how the setting shapes eating, from relaxed and open to quiet and controlled.

3.summary: Thirst: the temperature of food and drink that feels best.

4.summary: Touch: how busy or calm the eating setting is.

5.summary: Sound: how loud or quiet the surroundings are at meals.

6.summary: Light: how bright or shaded the surroundings are while eating.

1.summary: Caves: enclosed, sheltered surroundings that give a sense of privacy.

2.summary: Markets: busy places of exchange and social activity.

3.summary: Kitchens: warm, domestic places of nourishment and comfort.

4.summary: Mountains: elevated, open places with wide views.

5.summary: Valleys: low-lying, sheltered places surrounded by landscape.

6.summary: Shores: places at the border between land and water.

1.summary: Fear: caution and the wish for safety shape choices.

2.summary: Hope: expecting a good outcome draws you forward.

3.summary: Desire: a strong wish or craving moves you.

4.summary: Need: a sense of what is necessary drives action.

5.summary: Guilt: a sense of obligation and responsibility sets things in motion.

6.summary: Innocence: an open, unselfconscious drive moves you without agenda.

1.summary: Survival: sees through the lens of what keeps things safe and sustainable.

2.summary: Possibility: sees through the lens of what could happen.

3.summary: Power: sees through the lens of leverage and influence.

4.summary: Wanting: sees through the lens of what is desired.

5.summary: Probability: sees through the lens of what is likely to happen.

6.summary: Personal: sees through the lens of individual, lived experience.

digestion.summary: Left arrow: active and focused, with a selective approach to how things are taken in.

environment.summary: Left arrow: active and focused, with a deliberate approach to choosing surroundings.

motivation.summary: Left arrow: strategic and focused, driving toward a direct aim.

perspective.summary: Left arrow: strategic and focused, with a fixed point of view.

digestion.summary: Right arrow: receptive and peripheral, taking in what the setting provides.

environment.summary: Right arrow: receptive and peripheral, taking the surroundings as they come.

motivation.summary: Right arrow: receptive and peripheral, moved by what comes along.

perspective.summary: Right arrow: receptive and peripheral, with a wide field of view.

smell.name: Smell
smell.summary: Reads the atmosphere of places, people, and situations by sensing what feels fresh or off.

taste.name: Taste
taste.summary: Discerns by sampling, with a feel for quality, preference, and what suits.

outer_vision.name: Outer Vision
outer_vision.summary: Understands by observing what is in front of the eyes, seeing patterns in the outer world.

inner_vision.name: Inner Vision
inner_vision.summary: Understands through inner images, imagination, and mental pictures.

feeling.name: Feeling
feeling.summary: Knows through bodily and emotional sensing, picking up on subtle shifts.

touch.name: Touch
touch.summary: Knows through direct contact and physical experience of people and things.

shorthand.note: The code lists Personality first (Motivation, then Perspective), then Design (Digestion, then Environment). L stands for left and R for right.

individual.summary: The circuit of empowerment and uniqueness: people who bring new ideas, change, and their own distinctive voice.

collective_logic.summary: The circuit of sharing patterns: concerned with testing, refining, and passing on what works.

collective_abstract.summary: The circuit of sharing experience: feeling, memory, and storytelling as ways to learn from what has been lived.

tribal.summary: The circuit of support and loyalty: caring for family, community, resources, and mutual commitments.

knowing.summary: Individual stream of inner knowing and creative expression, often arriving as a unique contribution.

centering.summary: Individual stream of self-love, direction, and centered power from within.

integration.summary: Individual stream of self-reliance and present-time awareness for staying on your own path.

understanding.summary: Collective stream of logical pattern recognition: sharing what holds up and correcting what does not.

sensing.summary: Collective stream of felt experience, shared through stories and reflections on what happened.

ego.summary: Tribal stream of promises, resources, and bargains that hold a community together.

defense.summary: Tribal stream of care, bonding, and protection of the group and its boundaries.

right_angle.summary: Personal destiny: the life theme is lived through your own path, mostly shaped by your own experience.

juxtaposition.summary: Fixed destiny, seen only in the 4/1 profile: a consistent theme with a stable footing and little variation.

left_angle.summary: Transpersonal destiny: the life theme is lived through interactions with other people.

initiation.summary: First quarter, themed around Mind: purpose through initiating, thinking, and understanding.

civilization.summary: Second quarter, themed around Form: purpose through building, structure, and practical contribution.

duality.summary: Third quarter, themed around Bonding: purpose through relationships and the dance between two.

mutation.summary: Fourth quarter, themed around Transformation: purpose through change, evolution, and breaking old forms.

electromagnetic.name: Electromagnetic
electromagnetic.summary: Each person holds a different gate of the same channel. Together you complete it, and the framework links this to attraction.

companionship.name: Companionship
companionship.summary: You both hold the full channel. The framework links this to shared ease, familiarity, and a similar way of operating.

compromise.name: Compromise
compromise.summary: One person has the whole channel and the other holds one gate of it. The framework suggests the second adapts to the first.

dominance.name: Dominance
dominance.summary: One person has the whole channel and the other has neither gate. The framework links this to the full-channel person's steady influence.

composite.summary: The composite combines both charts to show which centers and channels are defined together. It is a symbolic lens, not a verdict on the relationship.

saturn_return.name: Saturn Return
saturn_return.summary: Around ages 29 to 30 and again near 59. Saturn returns to its birth position, traditionally a time to review responsibilities, structure, and direction.

uranus_opposition.name: Uranus Opposition
uranus_opposition.summary: Around age 42. Uranus opposes its birth position, traditionally a time of questioning the path and wanting more freedom.

chiron_return.name: Chiron Return
chiron_return.summary: Around age 50. Chiron returns to its birth position, traditionally linked to old wounds, wisdom, and the move into the third life phase.

uranus_return.name: Uranus Return
uranus_return.summary: Around age 84. Uranus completes its orbit, traditionally seen as the close of a full life cycle.

lunar.summary: The Moon travels through all 64 gates in about 28 days. Reflectors follow this cycle to see their own consistent patterns.

sensitivity.title: Birth time sensitivity
sensitivity.note: A small error in the birth time can change fast-moving or fine-grained details. Treat results near a boundary as uncertain.

orrery.label: Orrery
orrery.lede: The whole solar system from above the ecliptic, with real elliptical orbits. Switch to true scale to feel the actual distances.

moon.label: Sun · Earth · Moon
moon.lede: Why the Moon shows phases: its lit half always faces the Sun. The inset shows the same instant as seen from Earth.

eclipses.label: Eclipses
eclipses.lede: Umbra and penumbra cones drawn to scale. They stay faint until they meet the other body; that stamp is an eclipse.

retrograde.label: Retrograde
retrograde.lede: The planet's real path across the sky as seen from Earth. The inset shows Earth overtaking on the inside lane, which is what makes the loop.

why.solar_eclipse: The Moon's umbra reaches Earth: inside that narrow cone the Sun is fully covered, inside the penumbra only partly.
why.lunar_eclipse: The Moon crosses Earth's shadow. It only happens at full moon near a node, which is why it is not monthly.
why.moon_quarter: The phase is just how much of the lit half faces us: the Moon is always half lit by the Sun.
why.supermoon: A syzygy near perigee or apogee, so the Moon looks noticeably larger or smaller than usual.
why.moon_node: Where the tilted lunar orbit crosses the ecliptic. Eclipses cluster around these crossings.
why.season: The Sun crosses an equinox or reaches a solstice: Earth's 23.4° tilt, not its distance, drives the seasons.
why.apsis: The closest or farthest point of an orbit, a direct consequence of its ellipse.
why.elongation: The greatest angle from the Sun, when an inner planet is easiest to see after sunset or before sunrise.
why.peak_magnitude: The brightest moment, balancing distance against how much of the lit face we see.
why.opposition: Earth passes between the Sun and the planet: the planet is closest, brightest and visible all night.
why.conjunction: The planet lines up with the Sun as seen from Earth, so it is lost in the glare.
why.station: The moment the apparent motion reverses, as Earth overtakes the planet or is overtaken by it.
why.transit: The planet crosses the face of the Sun: a conjunction that happens to land close to a node.
why.pair_conjunction: Two bodies pass close together on the sky, though they stay far apart in space.
why.occultation: The Moon passes directly in front of the body, hiding it for a few minutes.

body.approximate_orbit: Position modelled from mean orbital elements, so the phase along the orbit is approximate; size, distance, period and direction are real.
